# trees

> A mock-up of the Intent UI idea (one document, many UI trees), skinned six ways: Kumo-like, terminal, System 7, Swiss print, LCARS and shadcn. It is not an IAP host.

- Live: https://trees.customer0.dev
- Source: https://github.com/acoyfellow/trees
- Based on: https://intent-ui.com (RFC: https://intent-ui.com/rfc) by Brayden Wilmoth

## What it shows

- Clicking a row or button marked as an unbuilt intent "builds" a page once (simulated model call, version bump).
- Switching skins, or opening two side by side, shows the built page with no new model calls.
- The JSON panel shows an illustrative IAP-style document that changes as you click.

## Caveats

- Not an IAP host: screens are hand-written Svelte; nothing is rendered from the JSON. No JSONata, source evaluation, validation or change pipeline.
- The JSON only loosely follows IAP v0.1; some fields (catalogVersion value, aliases shape) are made up.
- The six trees are CSS skins over one component set, not separate component libraries, so this does not test the catalog-agnostic claim.
- Model calls are simulated; there is no LLM behind it. Data is a fixed fixture.
